messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High-severity incident detected — GPU OOMs causing container restarts on prod-rt-2 during prefill. Route: /v1/generate. Region: us-west-2. Paging alex (oncall). Pager: #pagerduty :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): got the page, looking now. priya are you available?

priya (SRE): I’m on it. pulling logs from node-rt-12 and prod-rt-2. any customer reports? :eyes:

sara (support): Support has 3 customers reporting 5xx around 04:12 UTC, one major account (acme.ai) seeing repeated timeouts. I’m triaging.

daniel (runtime): Seen multiple container restarts on prod-rt-2. Prefill paths spike memory > 31GB, exit code 137. Looks like very long context prefill (user sent 64k token prompt).

priya (SRE): copying logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-14 04:12:23] runtime ERROR prefill: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.23GB
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. GPU 0 memory usage: 31.2/31.5 GB
Container exit: code 137 (killed)
Last kernel: aten::cublas_mm
Stack: /srv/runtime/serve.py:412 prefill
```

daniel (runtime): Confirmed. Prefill allocates KV cache sized for full context; we didn’t trim incoming system + long chat history. Model variant used: redwood/gpt-large@v3 (non-quantized).

alex (oncall): Immediate mitigation options? Can we evict long-prefill requests or route to smaller variant?

daniel (runtime): Can do a quick routing rule: requests with context_token_count > 4096 -> route to redwood/gpt-large-quant@v3 (4-bit) or block with 413 response. I can flip a runtime feature flag for us-west-2.

priya (SRE): I’ll cordon node-rt-12 to stop noisy restarts and drain instances. Also bump GPU pool capacity by +2 (autoscaler fallback) to give headroom.

ops-runner-bot: Scaling action initiated: add 2 gtx-a100 nodes to pool-prod-usw2-gpu. ETA ~ 6m.

sara (support): Noting customer impact: 5xx rate in us-west-2 spiked to 14% between 04:11–04:18 UTC. Acme.ai reported 120 failed requests. Informing account team.

niko (customer-success): looping in acct lead for Acme. They are in a critical demo window. Need ETA for mitigation and public status update.

daniel (runtime): Applying temporary prefill-trim middleware now (truncate user/system history to last 1024 tokens before allocating KV). Patching live on prod-rt-2 (canary first).

priya (SRE): Canary patch deployed to prod-rt-2-xyz (1 container). Monitoring.

incident-bot: NOTE: change window recorded. Change ID: chg_20260314_001.

(1m later)

daniel (runtime): Canary looks good — no OOM on canary for similar long requests (we simulated). Rolling to remaining containers in prod-rt-2 cluster.

priya (SRE): Node drain of node-rt-12 complete, container restarts stopped on that node. Scaling added nodes are provisioning (2/2 up).

ops-runner-bot: Added nodes are ready. Autoscaler metrics steady.

sara (support): 5xx rate reduced to 3% in us-west-2. Acme acknowledged mitigations, they saw reduced errors.

alex (oncall): Good. What’s root cause summary we’ll put in the incident timeline?

daniel (runtime): Root cause: Unbounded prefill allocation for very large user-provided context (64k tokens) caused KV cache allocation to exceed GPU memory for quantization-unfriendly model variant, leading to OOM and container SIGKILL (137). Contributing factors: no prefill-trim policy, routing to non-quantized model variant, and node capacity tightness.

priya (SRE): Live mitigations taken: 1) Deployed prefill-trim middleware (truncate to 1024 tokens) 2) Temporary routing rule to prefer quantized variant for large contexts in us-west-2 3) Cordoned/drained affected node 4) Scaled GPU pool +2 nodes 5) Added short prefill timeout (10s) to fail fast on oversized context.

sara (support): Customer impact: top customers affected: Acme.ai (120 failed reqs), BetaApps (34), internal e2e tests (CI jobs). No data loss, requests were retried by clients.

niko (customer-success): Sending quick status update to Acme: ETA for full remediation ~20–30m, root cause and mitigation steps summarized.

alex (oncall): Good work. Next steps: post-incident followup tasks — permanent prefill quota enforcement, add per-request KV allocation guard, improve model routing heuristics, add smoke test simulating large-context prefill to CI. Assign owners and timelines.

priya (SRE): I’ll own node capacity + autoscaler tuning (owner: priya).

daniel (runtime): I’ll own runtime guards + routing improvements (owner: daniel).

sara (support): I’ll prepare the customer-facing incident note and coordinate with acct teams (owner: sara).

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to P1->P2 after mitigations. Recording oncall handoff: alex -> next-night-oncall at 05:00 UTC.

alex (oncall): handing off to next oncall, leaving a short runbook in #oncall-runbooks. If anything regresses, ping me. :thumbsup:

priya (SRE): Leaving logs and timeline in the incident board. Will start a deeper postmortem tomorrow.

sara (support): Drafting a status update now. Will publish once reviewed.

daniel (runtime): Quick repro for postmortem: sending a synthetic 64k token prefill via internal loadgen produced OOM in 90s. Will attach artifacts.

niko (customer-success): Acme acknowledged and appreciated the update. They want a follow-up call tomorrow.

ops-runner-bot: Scheduler: create follow-up ticket: INF-2026-000123 (owner: daniel).

alex (oncall): closing live page. thanks team. :heart:
